# chapter: # Sources live in resources/sources/05/. Progress KB articles were recovered from archived copies of Progress's Salesforce article data; MDL Order 22 recites allegations, not findings.

claim as made in prose: On 31 May 2023 Progress warned MOVEit Transfer customers and posted fixes for supported versions
Earliest exploitation evidence was 27 May 2023, and data sometimes left within minutes of web-shell deployment
The input route was through session state, and the vulnerable lookup escaped one use of the email address but not another
source: rapid7-analysis-cve-2023-34362.txt, header-to-session narrative and published diff

claim as made in prose: The first patch changed the vulnerable function; SQL-injection advisories followed on 9 and 15 June
TechCrunch framed the event as a zero-day that let Clop raid MOVEit servers and steal customer data
TechTarget called CVE-2023-34362 a critical SQL-injection flaw and said instances were already under attack when Progress patched
A Progress spokesperson described a sophisticated multi-stage zero-day attack and said the 31 May patch fixed the issue
The quoted fixed-the-issue statement is carried by TechTarget rather than a Progress filing
Mandiant placed the earliest exploitation evidence on 27 May 2023
Progress received a support call on 28 May, contacted customers and took MOVEit Cloud down on 30 May, then patched and restored cloud service on 31 May
The earliest archived 31 May advisory told customers to block web traffic, inspect thirty days, and said SFTP and FTP/S would continue
Progress's revision history says supported fixes were posted 31 May; by 2 June the article named CVE-2023-34362 and described unauthenticated database access through SQL injection
CISA added CVE-2023-34362 to KEV on 2 June 2023 and marked ransomware campaign use known
CISA/FBI attributed the 27 May start to open-source information and described Clop exploiting the previously unknown flaw
CISA/FBI said the SQL-injection zero-day was used to install the LEMURLOOT web shell
Mandiant observed some theft within minutes, described the campaign as seemingly opportunistic, and merged UNC4857 into FIN11 based on overlaps
source: mandiant-2023-06-02.txt, update and opening incident summary

claim as made in prose: Rapid7 counted roughly 2,500 exposed MOVEit instances on 31 May; Huntress cited a Shodan result above 2,500
Emsisoft told TechTarget that 1,690 of 2,098 then-known victim organizations were compromised through third parties
Genworth reported 2.5 to 2.7 million policyholders affected through vendor PBI and said it did not itself use MOVEit
Emsisoft's June 2024 tally was 2,773 organizations and 95,788,491 individuals, with overlap it could not account for
KonBriefing says its sum is people records rather than distinct people and counts multiply affected people more than once
Rapid7 decompiled and diffed builds and found the first patch removed SetAllSessionVarsFromHeaders and rebuilt UserGetUsersWithEmailAddress
source: rapid7-analysis-cve-2023-34362.txt, first-patch analysis and published diff

claim as made in prose: Rapid7 found the removed function read X-siLock-SessVar pairs; logs and decompiled calls traced machine2.aspx loading session state and guestaccess.aspx reaching the vulnerable lookup
source: rapid7-analysis-cve-2023-34362.txt, header-to-session analysis and guestaccess call path

claim as made in prose: Progress's 9 June update said third-party review found distinct flaws; the advisory credits Huntress and assigns multiple SQL injections to CVE-2023-35036
Progress patched CVE-2023-35708 on 15 June after public posting and reported no evidence of exploitation
The July service pack added unauthenticated SQLi CVE-2023-36934 and authenticated SQLi CVE-2023-36932
Five SQL-injection CVE identifiers were patched over five weeks, and only CVE-2023-34362 is recorded in the saved sources as exploited before patching
Progress reported about 118 class actions and three formal government investigations in its January 2024 10-K
Progress reported in August 2024 that the SEC did not intend to recommend an enforcement action at that time
MDL Order 22 allowed some claims to proceed under Rule 12(b)(6), expressly treating the account as plaintiffs' allegations rather than findings
The old UserGetUsersWithEmailAddress format array held both an escaped email argument and the raw email argument
The pre-patch LIKE branches used escaped argument 1 while the equality clause Email='{2}' used raw argument 2
Rapid7 said naive attempts failed because the arguments on initially traced paths were escaped; session state led to the unescaped use
source: rapid7-analysis-cve-2023-34362.txt, narrative around query and guestaccess path

claim as made in prose: The patched function used SQLBasicBuilder, named parameters, and passed query plus parameter collection to DoReadQuery
The old DoReadQuery call received a completed SQL string; the patched call received generated query text and a parameter collection
Rapid7 traced session-loaded package data through four application calls to UserGetUsersWithEmailAddress
Rapid7's first-patch diff replaced string formatting with SQLBasicBuilder, four named bindings, and a query-plus-parameters read call
The first patch both parameterized the vulnerable lookup and removed the function that copied special headers into session state
source: rapid7-analysis-cve-2023-34362.txt, first-patch analysis and published diff

claim as made in prose: Progress said outside scrutiny produced additional findings and prompt patches, with no evidence of exploitation before those patches
CISA/FBI said its March 2024 alert responded to a publicized campaign against SQLi in a managed file-transfer application affecting thousands, without naming the product
CISA/FBI noted MySQL prepared statements in 2004 and others' treatment of SQLi as unforgivable since at least 2007
CISA/FBI recommended safe-by-default libraries, pull-request checks, and formal executive-sponsored code reviews
Progress said third-party code reviews, including Huntress's work, found additional vulnerabilities disclosed on 9 June
Progress announced a roughly two-month service-pack cadence in July and said the first pack fixed three new CVEs
Progress said on-premises MOVEit Transfer provides no continuing telemetry on version, file activity, or patch status
Rapid7's published diff shows one vulnerable function move from completed SQL-string construction to bound parameters
The zero-day SQL-injection label is supported by Progress's advisory, CVE/NVD/KEV records, and Rapid7's first-patch diff
Exploitation and some theft preceded Progress's 31 May patch; the response timeline runs from 27 to 31 May
TechTarget names the exploited CVE-2023-34362 but omits four later SQL-injection CVE identifiers that Progress patched over the next five weeks
Victim totals derive from an overlap-prone compilation, include records rather than deduplicated people, and mostly included third-party organizations at the cited point
The 31 May patch fixed CVE-2023-34362, while further parts of the chain and surrounding code were patched in June and July
Order 22 treated the alleged persistent SQLi as sufficient at pleading stage, not proven; Order 27 denied reconsideration
